events.title: Estonia's proposed eastern border closures are 'Russophobia,' Russian MFA says

articles.text: News ERR {{1794812100000 | amCalendar}} share Facebook X (Twitter) e-mail Maria Zakharova. Source: SCANPIX / ZUMAPRESS.com / Sergei Karpukhin News Moscow had called plans by Estonia to shut several of its eastern border crossings with Russia after a foiled arson attack attributed to Russia's military intellegence agency "Russophobia." Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) has asked the relevant authorities to prepare the next steps to close the border after a failed bid to start a fire at drone maker Threod Systems on Saturday morning. The Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS/ KAPO) said the act was carried out by residents of Latvia on the orders of Russia's GRU. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told state news agency TASS that if Estonia truly shut its border it would be yet another demonstration of Russophobia. "...If these are their real plans, then they fit into yet another bout of aggressive and unrestrained Russophobia," TASS quoted Zakharova as saying. The Estonian-Russian border runs through Lake Peipus. Border crossing points are highlighted on the map. Source: Helen Wright/ERR/OSM Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said road crossings on the Estonian-Russian border will shut on December 1. There are three crossing points on the border at Narva, Koidula, and Luhamaa. The government is set to discuss the issue later this week. It is not yet known whether the measure will be temporary or indefinite. Saturday's attempted arson attack is the second on a defense industry company in Estonia since August, when Milrem Robotics, which is based in Tallinn, was targeted. KAPO also attributed the incident to the GRU. Similar facilities have also been targeted across Europe as part of a campaign to reduce support for Ukraine and sow fear, the agency said. -- Follow ERR News on Facebook and Twitter and never miss an update! events.title: 8 detained after GRU-linked arson at Estonian drone company Threod Systems

articles.text: News ERR {{1794737160000 | amCalendar}} Updated: {{1794750060000 | amCalendar}} share Facebook X (Twitter) e-mail The Threod Factory in Viimsi. News Eight Latvian citizens have been detained after an attempted arson at Estonian drone manufacturer Threod Systems, which Estonia's domestic intellegence service has attributed to Russia's military intelligence agency, the GRU. Estonia is planning to close its eastern border in response. Prosecutor General Astrid Asi said at a press conference on Sunday that there was an attempt to break into Threod Systems' property in Viimsi, north of Tallinn, to start a fire at 3.06 a.m. on Saturday (November 14). The incident was thwarted thanks to the intervention of Threod's security team, Asi added. Internal Security Service (KAPO) Director General Margo Palloson said counterintelligence had confirmed that Russia was behind the attempted attack and that it was coordinated by Russia's military intelligence agency, the GRU. "This was yet another attempt by Russia to carry out an act of sabotage in Estonia," he told the assembled media. The attackers attempted to break the building's windows and pour flammable liquids inside to set the building on fire and cause an explosion, Palloson said. "We assess that if this attack had succeeded in the way the attackers planned, it would have caused very significant damage to the company," he said. Margo Palloson and the Prosecutor's Office. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR Palloson said no one was injured in the incident. The company did not suffer any significant damage, and the production and delivery capabilities were not affected, he added. Eight detained, five arrested Eight people have been detained, all residents of Latvia, by the Estonian Internal Security Service (KAPO) and the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA). "The Prosecutor's Office submitted an application to the court for the arrest of five suspects. The task of the criminal proceedings now is to establish the circumstances surrounding the organization of the attack, the roles of those involved and possible links to other individuals," Asi added. Palloson said Latvia's State Security Service (VDD) and Prosecutor's Office have contributed significantly to establishing the circumstances surrounding the case. Threod Systems produces both long-range reconnaissance and attack drones. This is the second known attempted arson attack on an Estonian defense company this year. Astrid Asi. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR In August, a fire was reported at defense contractor Milrem's office in Tallinn's Lasnamäe district, which KAPO also attributed to the Russian special services. Several Latvian citizens were also arrested in connection with the case. Several other defense industry companies across Europe have also been targeted in recent months. KAPO has said Russia is aiming to sow fear in society and among businesses, disrupt and weaken defense industry companies' production and technological development, and prevent defense industry products and technology from reaching Ukraine. Palloson explained that one of the GRU's methods is to recruit European Union residents who can move freely within the EU's Schengen Area to carry out physical attacks and acts of sabotage. Perpetrators are recruited from criminal circles and among people in difficult socioeconomic circumstances, he said. Estonia preparing to close Russian border Kristen Michal and Igor Taro. Source: Jürgen Randma/Government Office. Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) on Sunday requested that the "necessary steps" be taken to close Estonia's eastern border with Russia in response to the attacks. "Closing the border would reduce the threat to people in Estonia and send a clear message that attacks on Estonia's defence industry and defense capabilities are unacceptable," he said in a statement. Minister of the Interior Igor Taro (Eesti 200) said he will propose that all Estonia-Russia road border crossing points shut from the start of December. "Estonia has already significantly restricted traffic to and from Russia at our border crossing points, warning each time that further escalation could result in a complete closure of traffic. Now that moment has arrived," he said. Estonian citizens in Russia will have two weeks to return home, the minister added, It is not yet known if the closure will be temporary or indefinite. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Estonia's road borders will close on December 1. Estonia will close all Estonian-Russian border crossing points as of 1 December. Russia's attempts to intimidate, destabilise, or undermine our security will come with a price. We will take every necessary step to protect Estonia's security. — Estonian MFA | #StandWithUkraine (@MFAestonia) November 15, 2026 This story was updated to add comments from Internal Security Service (KAPO) Director General Margo Palloson and additional details about the incident. Then, for a second time, to add comments from Kristen Michal and Igor Taro. -- Follow ERR News on Facebook and Twitter and never miss an update!
